questions.question: Is emergency equipment on a bus required?

options.text: It is encouraged if there is extra room on the bus.
It is encouraged if there are more than 15 passengers.
Yes, it is required by law.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required by law.
questions.explanation: All commercial buses must have emergency equipment. This includes a fire extinguisher, emergency reflectors, and spare fuses if needed.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel sleepy while driving?

options.text: Keep driving to finish your trip.
Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Pull off the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel sleepy while driving, stop and get sleep. Trying to fight drowsiness is dangerous and causes many fatal crashes. Energy pills are not safe because they wear off quickly, making you even more tired than before.

questions.question: Why should you accelerate slowly when traction is poor?

options.text: Because you should always accelerate very slowly.
To keep control of your vehicle.
So you do not go faster than the vehicle ahead.
To be the last vehicle through an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep control of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up too quickly on a slippery road can cause you to lose control. When traction is poor, accelerate slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: Why should charter bus passengers board at departure time only?

options.text: It saves money because bus charges start when the first person boards.
Early boarding leads to passengers getting on and off multiple times, risking missing the departure.
Passengers should not choose their own seats until departure time.
It helps prevent theft and damage to the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps prevent theft and damage to the bus.
questions.explanation: Charter bus drivers should only allow passengers to board at departure time. This helps prevent theft and vandalism.

questions.question: What do federal and state laws require drivers to do?

options.text: Inspect their vehicles only if they think there is a problem.
Inspect their vehicles only when traveling out-of-state.
Inspect their vehicles only when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require commercial drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip. Regular inspections help drivers find problems before they become dangerous or costly.

questions.question: Is texting while driving a commercial vehicle allowed?

options.text: Yes, if the message has fewer than 10 words.
Yes, because it is safer than talking on the phone.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving a commercial vehicle is illegal and dangerous. This includes typing messages or reading messages on any electronic device.

questions.question: What task might a CDL applicant be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?
questions.explanation: The CDL vehicle inspection test includes a full vehicle check. One required task is checking the engine oil level.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a curve on the skills test?

options.text: Leave your lane if needed to complete the curve.
Slow down after entering the curve.
Stop checking for other vehicles while turning.
Slow down before entering the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Before entering a curve, slow down enough so you do not need to brake or shift while in the curve. Stay in your lane and watch for traffic in all directions.

questions.question: Which is an example of required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes: at least one fire extinguisher; spare electrical fuses (unless your vehicle has circuit breakers); and warning devices for parked vehicles (such as reflective triangles).

questions.question: With low beam headlights on, how far ahead can you see?
questions.explanation: Low beam headlights let you see about 250 feet ahead. When driving at night, adjust your speed so you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, repeated yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, wandering thoughts, and drifting out of your lane.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles need ____ to change gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions use double clutching to change gears. Release the accelerator, push in the clutch, and shift to neutral at the same time. Release the clutch and let the vehicle reach the right speed. Then push the clutch in, shift gears, and release the clutch while accelerating.

questions.question: How far your vehicle stops can be affected by:
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your speed, vehicle weight, and how slippery the road is.

questions.question: When carrying cargo, you must check that it is secure:

options.text: Every 150 miles or three hours of driving.
Only after traveling up a hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles or three hours of driving.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safe and secure throughout the trip.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road
A thin layer of ice on the road
Ice that is black from road debris
Ice that is easy to see

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road surface through it. A road with black ice may just look wet.

questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked correctly if:

options.text: There is no trailer attached to the tractor.
The vehicle is on a slight incline.
The vehicle is on a slight decline.

questions.explanation: When a trailer is attached to a tractor, mirrors can only be adjusted properly if the trailer is straight.

questions.question: Which surface gives the least traction?
questions.explanation: Be very careful when driving on melting ice. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: When you start the vehicle during the pre-trip inspection, the coolant temperature should:
questions.explanation: After starting your vehicle during the pre-trip inspection, watch the gauges. The coolant temperature should gradually rise to normal operating range.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, you:

options.text: Must keep four points of contact with the vehicle.
May turn to face the road before exiting is complete.
Must face away from the vehicle.

questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. If your vehicle is a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may result in failing the basic control skills test.

questions.question: If there are no warning gates or lights at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Not worry because the tracks are likely abandoned.
Park and walk to the tracks to check for approaching trains.
Look both ways down the tracks to make sure no trains are coming.
Do whatever the other vehicles are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look both ways down the tracks to make sure no trains are coming.
questions.explanation: A passive railroad crossing has no gates or warning lights. Before crossing, look both directions down the tracks to check for approaching trains.
